evals.prompt: The operator says: commit the parser fix. The current task changed parser.py and test_parser.py. notes.md has an unrelated unstaged edit. Nothing is staged. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Stages only parser.py and test_parser.py, reviews the staged diff, creates one local commit with a parser-focused subject, verifies both committed paths, and leaves notes.md unstaged. It does not ask the operator to stage files or push.
assertions: Stages the two task-owned files without staging notes.md
Does not ask the operator to curate an empty index
Creates exactly one local commit and does not push
Verifies unrelated unstaged work remains

evals.prompt: The operator says: commit this new skill. The skill directory is wholly new. A generated registry contains the new skill row plus unrelated rows changed by another task. Other files are dirty. Nothing is staged. Describe the exact commit behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Stages the new skill directory with explicit paths and only its registry row using a cached patch. It reviews the isolated index, commits once, and verifies other registry edits and dirty files remain uncommitted.
assertions: Stages the whole owned skill package with explicit paths
Stages only the owned registry row rather than the whole registry
Does not use a broad git add pathspec
Verifies unrelated registry and worktree changes remain

evals.prompt: The operator asks to commit one fix, but an already-staged hunk combines that fix with another person's edit on the same lines. The ownership cannot be separated safely from available context. Describe the behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Stops before committing, reports the exact inseparable staged hunk as a boundary blocker, preserves the index and worktree, and does not reset, unstage, commit, or push.
assertions: Returns a specific boundary blocker
Does not commit the mixed hunk
Does not reset or alter the existing index
Does not push

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared worktree on local main. The operator says: commit this and push. origin/main gained one commit since the last fetch, and other threads have staged and unstaged edits in the worktree. The repository is public. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Creates one isolated commit from explicit paths or hunks, fetches origin/main, and because the index holds other threads' staged work, builds one merge commit with merge-tree and commit-tree after confirming the incoming paths do not overlap local changes, refreshing only those paths. It lists every outgoing commit, scans the outgoing diff for secrets and private data, pushes main straight to origin/main without force or rebase, verifies origin/main equals HEAD, and reports the published commits. It opens no PR.
assertions: Pushes main directly to origin/main and opens no PR
Integrates the moved origin/main with a merge commit, never a rebase or force push
Preserves other threads' staged and unstaged work
Scans the outgoing range for secrets and private data before pushing a public repo
Verifies origin/main equals HEAD and names the published commits

farplane.title: Push: straight to main after origin moved

evals.prompt: Farplane uses one shared worktree on local main. The operator asks to commit the current isolated change and open a PR. Describe the exact Git behavior without running commands.
evals.expected_output: Creates one isolated commit, then follows the single-worktree PR route: pushes HEAD to a temporary remote codex branch without creating or switching a local branch, opens the PR against main, and does not push main directly.
assertions: Pushes HEAD to refs/heads/codex/<task-name> without a local branch switch
Opens the PR against main
Does not push main directly when a PR was requested
